newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defense attacks witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defense attacks witnesses.

text.p: Attorneys for Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh launched an attack Wednesday on the reliability of witnesses whose testimony prosecutors plan to use to obtain a conviction.
The attorneys, in a written filing, asked the trial judge to suppress the testimony of seven witnesses, arguing that the government's procedures were tainted.
"None of the potential witnesses the government will call at trial can make a positive identification of Mr. McVeigh," his lawyers said.
The identification is tainted, in part, because some of the witnesses saw news photos of McVeigh before being asked by authorities to identify him, McVeigh's lawyers alleged.
Prosecutor Scott Mendeloff denied the identification process was tainted and said the government will respond more fully at a later date.

According to the defence filing only one of the prosecution's witnesses claims to possibly have seen McVeigh and a Ryder rental truck in front of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building just before a truck bomb exploded in 1995.

McVeigh and former Army buddy Terry Nichols are accused of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that killed 168 people. McVeigh goes on trial March 31 and Nichols at a later date. Both face the death penalty if convicted.

In a surprise move, Nichols' attorney Michael Tigar in a filing asked the court to disqualify two prosecutors. Tigar said he may have to question the prosecutors on the witness stand about claims prosecutors tried to get witnesses to charge their stories. Attorneys can not both participate in a case and offer testimony in the same case.
Prosecutors in a late filing called the charge "strident" and "baseless" and said the two government attorneys, Mendeloff and Larry Mackey have "exceeded the aplicable ethics rules."
